Verify Now Blog > Corporate Social Responsibility of PCBWay Corporate Social Responsibility of PCBWay by: PCBWay May 30,2025 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News PCBWay recognizes the significant role it plays within the supply chain and broader society, along with the potential impact of its operations. To this end, we have established and strictly enforce the following principles, which not only govern our own conduct but also set clear expectations for our partners. Our goal is to ensure full legal and regulatory compliance, promote long-term sustainability, and generate a positive impact on society. Human Rights and Labor Protection No employment of individuals below the legal working age; all forms of forced or bonded labor are strictly prohibited. Discrimination and harassment in the workplace are not tolerated; an inclusive work environment for persons with disabilities is encouraged. Employees must be provided with fair compensation and reasonable rest periods, and their rights to freedom of association and collective bargaining must be respected. Business Ethics and Compliance Offering, promising, soliciting, or accepting any form of bribery is strictly prohibited; effective conflict of interest management and whistleblowing mechanisms must be in place. All financial and business records must accurately, completely, and truthfully reflect the underlying transactions. Full compliance with international sanctions, export controls, and other applicable laws and regulations is required. Supply Chain Responsibility and Sustainable Procurement PCBWay and its partners are required to extend the principles outlined in this document to all levels of entities within the supply chain. Priority should be given to selecting partners that are legally compliant, socially responsible, and committed to sustainable development. Identify social, labor, and environmental risks related to operations, and develop corresponding control and mitigation measures. Encourage partners to prioritize local sourcing to support regional economic development and job creation. Environmental Protection and Workplace Safety Actively implement environmental protection measures and continuously promote energy conservation and emission reduction; Ensure that all waste and hazardous materials are disposed of in accordance with relevant laws and regulations. The procurement or use of prohibited materials is not allowed. Provide employees with a safe working environment and health support mechanisms to prevent occupational injuries and health risks. PCBWay has fully adopted the DHL GoGreen transportation service in 2025 to reduce carbon emissions in the supply chain and promote the development of a green supply chain, with an initial target of reducing emissions by 30%. Information Protection and Transparent Governance Establish a comprehensive security system to strictly protect the confidentiality of customer data, drawings, and other business information. Comply with relevant laws and regulations to safeguard the personal data of customers and employees. Ensure that financial records are true, accurate, and complete, and prohibit any illegal activities. PCBWay will ensure the implementation of the above principles in actual cooperation and reserves the right to take action against any violations. DHL may contact recipients for required documentation/clarification to clear shipments (regardless of Incoterm® used). Global Direct Shipping Duties included in shipping costs. Global Direct Shipping is likely the most cost-effective option. Duties are included in the shipping cost, avoiding unexpected fees. Best for lower-value shipments (max declared value: $60 USD per package). No need for additional tax disputes or refund processes. If your shipment meets the value limit, this is the simplest and most economical choice. 4. Global Standard Shipping, USPS Prepaid tax fee: A 30% duty rate (based on declared value) will be charged upon package arrival. No refunds, no additional charges, and no tax invoice provided. For further inquiries, please contact: logistics@pcbway.com Update on May 12th The Government of the United States of America (the “United States”) and the Government of the People’s Republic of China (“China”), Recognizing the importance of their bilateral economic and trade relationship to both countries and the global economy; Recognizing the importance of a sustainable, long-term, and mutually beneficial economic and trade relationship; Reflecting on their recent discussions and believing that continued discussions have the potential to address the concerns of each side in their economic and trade relationship; and Moving forward in the spirit of mutual opening, continued communication, cooperation, and mutual respect; The Parties commit to take the following actions by May 14, 2025 : The United States will (i) modify the application of the additional ad valorem rate of duty on articles of China (including articles of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the Macau Special Administrative Region) set forth in Executive Order 14257 of April 2, 2025, by suspending 24 percentage points of that rate for an initial period of 90 days, while retaining the remaining ad valorem rate of 10 percent on those articles pursuant to the terms of said Order; and (ii) removing the modified additional ad valorem rates of duty on those articles imposed by Executive Order 14259 of April 8, 2025 and Executive Order 14266 of April 9, 2025. China will (i) modify accordingly the application of the additional ad valorem rate of duty on articles of the United States set forth in Announcement of the Customs Tariff Commission of the State Council No. 4 of 2025, by suspending 24 percentage points of that rate for an initial period of 90 days, while retaining the remaining additional ad valorem rate of 10 percent on those articles, and removing the modified additional ad valorem rates of duty on those articles imposed by Announcement of the Customs Tariff Commission of the State Council No. 5 of 2025 and Announcement of the Customs Tariff Commission of the State Council No. 6 of 2025; and (ii) adopt all necessary administrative measures to suspend or remove the non-tariff countermeasures taken against the United States since April 2, 2025. After taking the aforementioned actions, the Parties will establish a mechanism to continue discussions about economic and trade relations. The representative from the Chinese side for these discussions will be He Lifeng, Vice Premier of the State Council, and the representatives from the U.S. side will be Scott Bessent, Secretary of the Treasury, and Jamieson Greer, United States Trade Representative. These discussions may be conducted alternately in China and the United States, or a third country upon agreement of the Parties. As required, the two sides may conduct working-level consultations on relevant economic and trade issues. https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefings-statements/2025/05/joint-statement-on-u-s-china-economic-and-trade-meeting-in-geneva/ Updated on April 25th **Presidential Executive Order on Tariff Adjustments for Chinese Goods** On April 8, 2025 (local time), U.S. President Donald Trump issued an executive order announcing the following tariff measures on goods originating from China (including Hong Kong, China): 1. **Elimination of De Minimis Exemption for Chinese-origin Goods** 2. **Additional 125%+20% (If it is the category under 9903.01.32 or 9903.01.33, the tariff exemption is 125%) Tariff on High-value Chinese Goods** 3.Fedex Official: For B2C shipments, a valid FedEx account number is required. 4.If the product falls under HTS categories 9903.01.32 or 9903.01.33, it qualifies for a 125% tariff exemption. However, DHL’s customs declaration system may inaccurately apply or fail to recognize the 125% exemption. If the recipient finds that the product is indeed eligible for the exemption but the 125% duty relief was not applied, they must file a dispute with DHL immediately, as there is a strict deadline for appeals. By the time the sender notices the issue, the appeal window may have already closed. Note: Regarding why your social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number is needed when shipping, please check out this official article for explanation: Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? ============================================================================================== by the way： Importers - Why is an overseas supplier asking for my social security number/tax ID number/IRS number/importer number? When an individual or company purchases goods from an overseas supplier, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) considers them the ultimate importer. The ultimate importer can clear the goods or have a Customs Broker clear them on their behalf. If the supplier hires a carrier that provides door to door service, the carrier service usually has brokers in their supply chain to clear the goods on behalf of the ultimate importer. If a formal entry is required, CBP regulations require the broker to put the ultimate importer's identification number on the CBP Form 7501- Entry Summary. The ultimate importer's identification number is either the Employers Identification Number (EIN) tax identification number assigned by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or the importer's social security number. The EIN is issued for the purpose of tax administration and are not intended for participation in any other activities (e.g., tax lien auction or sales, lotteries). For additional information about EIN, please visit the IRS web page "Apply for an Employer Identification (EIN) Online." Goods are usually cleared informally when they are for personal use, under $2500 in value, and are not in commercial quantities. A formal entry is usually required for commercial importations valued over $2,500. Because many foreign merchants are aware that CBP requires an identification number for the ultimate importer for formal entries, they will often request the purchaser's social security number to include on export documents that the broker will subsequently rely on to prepare the CBP entry. It should be noted that paperwork for goods sent by courier service does ask for an importer number, whether the import qualifies for an informal entry or not. Courier services file CBP entries electronically, and the software system they use requires an identification number to be provided for the recipient of the goods. If an identification number is not provided, the courier service is required to file a paper entry, which is extremely time-consuming and in the world of "Overnight Delivery" not practical. The end result is that most courier services will not accept packages for international delivery to U.S. residents if a recipient's identification number is not provided by the shipper. When an individual or company purchases goods from an overseas supplier, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) considers them the ultimate importer. The ultimate importer can clear the goods or have a Customs Broker clear them on their behalf. If the supplier hires a carrier that provides door to door service, the carrier service usually has brokers in their supply chain to clear the goods on behalf of the ultimate importer. If a formal entry is required, CBP regulations require the broker to put the ultimate importer's identification number on the CBP Form 7501- Entry Summary. The ultimate importer's identification number is either the Employers Identification Number (EIN) tax identification number assigned by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or the importer's social security number. The EIN is issued for the purpose of tax administration and are not intended for participation in any other activities (e.g., tax lien auction or sales, lotteries). For additional information about EIN, please visit the IRS web page "Apply for an Employer Identification (EIN) Online." Goods are usually cleared informally when they are for personal use, under $2500 in value, and are not in commercial quantities. A formal entry is usually required for commercial importations valued over $2,500. Because many foreign merchants are aware that CBP requires an identification number for the ultimate importer for formal entries, they will often request the purchaser's social security number to include on export documents that the broker will subsequently rely on to prepare the CBP entry. It should be noted that paperwork for goods sent by courier service does ask for an importer number, whether the import qualifies for an informal entry or not. Courier services file CBP entries electronically, and the software system they use requires an identification number to be provided for the recipient of the goods. If an identification number is not provided, the courier service is required to file a paper entry, which is extremely time-consuming and in the world of "Overnight Delivery" not practical. The end result is that most courier services will not accept packages for international delivery to U.S. residents if a recipient's identification number is not provided by the shipper. Goods sent through the international postal service that are under $2500 in value generally do not require an importer number to be cleared through CBP. Shipments arriving after this time or declared for arrival after this time are subject to the order. The "$800 de minimis exemption" and the "T86 clearance model" no longer apply.As a result, shipments from PCBWay to the U.S. will incur additional tariffs. Meet PCBWay at electronica 2024! by: PCBWay Oct 18,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Once again, we welcome the famous technology event electronica in Munich, Germany! Since the first exhibition was held in 1964, electronica has gradually grown and now covers the entire world of electronics, including the micro- and nano-worlds of semiconductor and micro systems technology, as well as measurement and sensor technology, display technology and vehicle electronics, etc., which is the best choice for any technology enthusiasts and industry practitioners. PCBWay has participated in theelectronica many times and has received a warm response every time. At the exhibition, everyone has the opportunity to get close to our various products and fully evaluate the performance and quality of our products, which is far beyond the scope of online communication. On-site interaction gives us the opportunity to answer everyone's questions in a timely manner and help them understand the products more comprehensively, thereby accelerating the process of cooperation. Therefore, after the exhibition, we not only strengthened our cooperation with existing customers, but also successfully attracted the attention of many new potential partners. PCBWay will certainly not be absent from this year's exhibition.In addition, in order to give everyone a better exhibition experience and also to show how much importance PCBWay attaches to this exhibition, this year we made some innovations: Time: 2024.11.12-2024.11.15 Location: Trade Fair Center Messe München, Germany PCBWay Booth No.: A1.163 Highlights: Color- printed Boards In addition to the PCB series products, 3D printed parts and sheet metal parts that we have been displaying in the past, we will also bring the latest color-printed board samples. This new product has attracted the attention and interest of many customers, so we hope to take this opportunity to let everyone experience the excellent effect and quality of the color-printed board in person. New Booth We focused on designing the on-site booth as well. We expanded the booth area to 5m x 14m, providing a larger activity space, and also improved the sophistication of various details, in order to make the overall atmosphere more professional and make everyone's visiting experience more comfortable. The final booth design renderings are as follows: Gifts We will also bring some small gifts to the exhibition, including water cups, neck masks, and T-shirts. Welcome to come and get them! Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Fabrication Toolkit for Kicad PCBWay Fabrication Toolkit for Kicad by: PCBWay Oct 11,2023 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Recently, PCBWay added a plug-in called PCBWay Fabrication Toolkit to Kicad: With just one click of the mouse, four files can be exported from the layout file automatically: Gerber file, IPC-Netlist file, BOM file and Pick and Place file, which can significantly improves the efficiency of pre-production work. Installation from the Official KiCad Repositories After installation, the plugin will appear on the right side of the navigation bar. And users can use it to export all the production files with just a click. Process demonstration： Sending the files to PCBWay, and they can be used for production after being reviewed by the staff. Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad by: Anson Apr 01,2022 Posted in News Kicad PCB design Send your layout to PCBWay for instant production with just one click. Have you ever thought that when you complete the design on KiCad, you can place an order on pcbway with just one click? Now this idea is finally achieved (it's not an April Fool's joke). When you click PCBWay Plug-in button on Kicad, we will export these files in your project ( Please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin released at 2026 )： 1.Gerber files in correct format for production 2.IPC-Netlist file 3.Bom-file that includes all information of components 4.Pick and Place-file used in assembly You can click "Save to Cart" to place an order immediately after uploading the files( usually only takes a few seconds), our engineers will double check the files before the production. Note:We have updated plugin for Kicad 10,you could also place assembly order directly now. But we need to get the component "Manufacture Part Number". Please confirm you run the "Update Board from Schematic" and install the latest version of the plugin. ﻿ Installation from the official KiCad repositories Just open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the KiCad main menu an install the "PCBWay Plug-in for KiCad" plugin from the selection list. Manual installation You can also download the latest ZIP file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Plug-in-for-Kicad , then open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the main window of KiCad and install the ZIP file via "Install from File". About Bom We can get all information of components used in your design ( please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin) . In order to speed up the quotation of components, we need this information: 1. Designator (necessary) 2. Quantity (necessary) 3. MPN/Part Number (necessary) 4. Package/Footprint (necessary) 5. Manufacturer (optional) 6. Description/value (optional) You just need to add the properties in your schematic like the picture shows: As a sponsor of KiCad, we will always support its development. Verify Now Blog > PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad PCBWay Plug-In for KiCad by: Anson Apr 01,2022 Posted in News Kicad PCB design Send your layout to PCBWay for instant production with just one click. Have you ever thought that when you complete the design on KiCad, you can place an order on pcbway with just one click? Now this idea is finally achieved (it's not an April Fool's joke). When you click PCBWay Plug-in button on Kicad, we will export these files in your project ( Please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin released at 2026 )： 1.Gerber files in correct format for production 2.IPC-Netlist file 3.Bom-file that includes all information of components 4.Pick and Place-file used in assembly You can click "Save to Cart" to place an order immediately after uploading the files( usually only takes a few seconds), our engineers will double check the files before the production. Note:We have updated plugin for Kicad 10,you could also place assembly order directly now. But we need to get the component "Manufacture Part Number". Please confirm you run the "Update Board from Schematic" and install the latest version of the plugin. ﻿ Installation from the official KiCad repositories Just open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the KiCad main menu an install the "PCBWay Plug-in for KiCad" plugin from the selection list. Manual installation You can also download the latest ZIP file from https://github.com/pcbway/PCBWay-Plug-in-for-Kicad , then open the "Plugin and Content Manager" from the main window of KiCad and install the ZIP file via "Install from File". About Bom We can get all information of components used in your design ( please make sure you have installed the latest version of the plugin) . In order to speed up the quotation of components, we need this information: 1. Designator (necessary) 2. Quantity (necessary) 3. MPN/Part Number (necessary) 4. Package/Footprint (necessary) 5. Manufacturer (optional) 6. Description/value (optional) You just need to add the properties in your schematic like the picture shows: As a sponsor of KiCad, we will always support its development. Note: Thanks to the open source community. Since we are not skilled enough to edit on github at the moment, any feedback or questions please contact with anson@pcbway.com Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Join us Wanna be a dedicated PCBWay writer? We definately look forward to having you with us. get_components_file(self, temp_dir): if hasattr(self.board, 'GetModules'): footprints = list(self.board.GetModules()) else: footprints = list(self.board.GetFootprints()) footprints.sort(key=lambda x: x.GetReference()) for i, f in enumerate(footprints): try: footprint_name = str(f.GetFPID().GetFootprintName()) except AttributeError: footprint_name = str(f.GetFPID().GetLibItemName()) layer = { pcbnew.F_Cu: 'top', pcbnew.B_Cu: 'bottom', }.get(f.GetLayer()) f_attrs = f.GetAttributes() parsed_attrs = self.parse_attrs(f_attrs) mount_type = 'smt' if parsed_attrs['smd'] else 'tht' placed = not parsed_attrs['not_in_bom'] rotation = f.GetOrientation().AsDegrees() if hasattr(f.GetOrientation(), 'AsDegrees') else f.GetOrientation() / 10.0 designator = f.GetReference() pos_x = (f.GetPosition()[0] - self.board.GetDesignSettings().GetAuxOrigin()[0]) / 1000000.0 pos_y = (f.GetPosition()[1] - self.board.GetDesignSettings().GetAuxOrigin()[1]) * -1.0 / 1000000.0 mpn = is_exist_bom == False and placed == True: self.bom.append({ 'designator': designator, 'quantity': 1, 'value': value, 'pack': footprint_name, 'mpn': mpn, 'mount_type': mount_type }) if len(self.components) > 0: with open((os.path.join(temp_dir, positionsFilename)), 'w', newline='', encoding='utf-8-sig') as outfile: csvobj = csv.writer(outfile) in component['designator']): csvobj.writerow(component.values()) def get_gerber_parameter(self): boardWidth = pcbnew.ToMM(self.board.GetBoardEdgesBoundingBox().GetWidth()) boardHeight = pcbnew.ToMM(self.board.GetBoardEdgesBoundingBox().GetHeight()) if hasattr(self.board, 'GetCopperLayerCount'): boardLayer = self.board.GetCopperLayerCount() gerberData = {'boardWidth':boardWidth,'boardHeight':boardHeight,'boardLayer':boardLayer} return gerberData def get_name(self): p_name = self.board.GetFileName() return p_name def parse_attrs(self, attrs): return {} if not isinstance(attrs, int) else { 'tht': self.parse_attr_flag(attrs, pcbnew.FP_THROUGH_HOLE), 'smd': self.parse_attr_flag(attrs, pcbnew.FP_SMD), 'not_in_pos': self.parse_attr_flag(attrs, get_mpn_from_footprint(self, f): keys = ['mpn', 'MPN', 'Mpn', 'PCBWay_MPN' ,'part number', 'Part Number', 'Part No.', 'Mfr. Part No.', 'Mfg Part'] for key in keys: try: if f.HasField(key): return f.GetFieldByName(key).GetText() except Exception as e: if f.HasProperty(key): return f.GetProperty(key) def get_pack_from_footprint(self, f): keys = ['pack', 'PACK', 'Pack', 'package' ,'PACKAGE', 'Package', 'case', 'CASE', 'Case'] for key in keys: try: if f.HasField(key): return f.GetFieldByName(key).GetText() except Exception as e: if f.HasProperty(key): return f.GetProperty(key) def parse_attr_flag(self, attr, mask): return mask == (attr & mask) Upload photo 0 /10000 You can upload up to 5 images! Unlock Color PCB Printing with PCBWay! by: PCBWay Mar 08,2024 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in News Color PCB Printing PCBWay Service Nowadays, traditional PCB printing technology can no longer meet the aesthetic requirements of modern circuit board production. To better fulfill customers' design needs, we are pleased to announce that PCBWay has introduced UV printing equipment. This equipment utilizes UV-curable inks to achieve high-quality image printing on various materials, including fiberglass boards, metal substrates, ceramic substrates, flexible boards, and rigid-flex boards. Entrance https://www.pcbway.com/orderonline.aspx Prerequisites for Ordering Maximum size for a single piece: 270*470MM; Selection of background soldermask color required. Design Specifications Drill holes, traces, soldermasks, and outline designs must comply with specifications. Avoid placing colored characters in areas with solder mask openings, such as surface-mount pads or through-hole pads. What kind of files should be provided for color printing? Method One : Draw colored characters on the silkscreen layer of the Gerber and provide reference pictures. For example: Method Two : If you include information about colored silkscreen in the Gerber layer, each individual color must have its own layer. If there is only one layer, we can only print one color. [This method is not recommended] . If you need to print in multiple colors, we recommend using method One and providing us with a reference picture. 4.Please send the images you want to print on the PCB in the following formats: AI, PDF, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, etc., and indicate your desired printing location on the board. 5.If the image contains a QR code, please ensure that the QR code can be accurately scanned and recognized. Note : If you choose UV printing Multi-color, we will use matte UV color printing by default. When designing the colored characters on the bottom layer, be careful not to design the colored characters as mirrored inverses. (The process of color printing is different from that of standard PCB silkscreen printing. When printing colorful characters on the bottom layer, they are printed with the bottom layer of the PCB facing up.) For situations where the entire top or bottom side requires full-color printing, regardless of the solder mask color you choose, we will use a white solder mask on the full-color printed side and then proceed with the color printing. This is for a better printing effect. Please upload the print image, positioning image, and Gerber in one compressed file. By providing a clear positioning image and necessary instructions, you can assist PCBWay in accurately determining and achieving the desired printing position. Matte UV Color Printing vs. Glossy UV Color Printing Matte ink does not increase the overall thickness, and the PCB's appearance looks smooth. Glossy ink increases the overall thickness and may affect the soldering of component pads. The appearance is beautiful but uneven. Features Adopting UV-LED lamp curing, which enables instant drying, can significantly enhances production efficiency. UV printing technology employs UV-curable inks, ensuring firm and clear printing information resistant to fading, thus enhancing product identification and aesthetics. The normal print survives SMT reflow. UV printing technology can present images in various colors and styles, meeting customers' personalized requirements. Professional industrial-grade UV printers support high-precision printing, delivering exquisite results whether on flat panels or rolled materials. Unlike traditional printing methods, UV printing does not produce volatile organic compounds during the production process, ensuring air quality in the production workshop and providing employees with a safer and healthier working environment. FAQ on UV Printing: Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with water? Yes, it can be cleaned with water. Can the UV printed surface be cleaned with alcohol? It is more difficult to clean after being exposed to alcohol and baked (currently, the board undergoes a short baking process after UV printing). However, with increased contact time with alcohol and vigorous scrubbing, it can be removed. This also depends on whether the UV is on the copper surface or the solder mask surface. How hard is the UV printed surface (sensitivity to scratches)? The UV surface is not sensitive to scratches. However, compared to the solder mask, it is less scratch-resistant because UV printing is ink that is sprayed on and is relatively thin. Welcome to give it a try if you're interested! Besides, PCBWay will continue to enhance its manufacturing capabilities to bring more choices and personalized services to customers in the future. Verify Now Blog > How to Get $29 PCB Assembly and Meet the Requirements How to Get $29 PCB Assembly and Meet the Requirements by: Mila Oct 21,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Assembly PCBWay's $29 PCB assembly offer provides a special assembly service price for eligible PCB prototypes. It is designed for relatively simple projects with limited assembly requirements. Not every PCB assembly project qualifies for this offer. Your project must meet the technical requirements listed below, and the promotion is subject to customer eligibility and usage limits. $29 PCB Assembly Requirements To qualify for the $29 PCB assembly offer, your project must meet all of the following requirements: Component Sourcing: All components must be supplied by PCBWay. PCB Type: Only rigid PCBs are eligible. Flex PCBs and rigid-flex PCBs are not supported by this offer. Assembly Quantity: No more than 20 boards per order. Components per Board: Each board can have a maximum of 200 components. Total Component Quantity: The total number of components across the order cannot exceed 600. Unique Component Types: The project can include no more than 100 different component types. Through-Hole Solder Joints: The total number of through-hole solder joints cannot exceed 100. All limits are inclusive. For example, an order for exactly 20 boards or a project with exactly 100 different component types can qualify, provided that all other requirements are also met. Important: Meeting these technical requirements does not automatically guarantee the promotional price. Your order must also meet the applicable customer eligibility and monthly usage limits. How Often Can You Use the $29 PCB Assembly Offer? The $29 PCB assembly promotion has a monthly usage limit based on customer status. New customers: Eligible new customers can use the offer once per month. Returning customers: Eligible returning customers can use the offer up to twice per month. If you submit multiple orders at the same time, only one eligible order can receive the $29 promotional price. The remaining orders will be charged at their applicable rates. Please note that each order must meet all the technical requirements to qualify for the promotion. The monthly usage limit does not mean that every order you submit will receive the special price. How to Get $29 PCB Assembly on PCBWay Follow these steps to get started. Step 1: Prepare your PCB design files Prepare your Gerber files, Bill of Materials (BOM), and pick-and-place file, as applicable to your project. Step 2: Check your project requirements Confirm that your project uses rigid PCBs, that all components will be supplied by PCBWay, and that your assembly quantity and component counts are within the specified limits. Step 3: Submit your assembly order Visit the PCBWay PCB Assembly Service page and submit your PCB assembly files and requirements. Step 4: Confirm your eligibility Check your eligibility for the promotion and make sure you have not exceeded the applicable usage limit. The final price is subject to order review and confirmation. Frequently Asked Questions -Can I use the $29 PCB assembly offer for flex PCBs or rigid-flex PCBs? No. The promotion is available for rigid PCBs only. Flex PCBs and rigid-flex PCBs are excluded. -Can I supply my own components? No. All components must be supplied by PCBWay to qualify for this offer. -Can I order more than 20 boards? No. The maximum eligible assembly quantity is 20 boards per order. -How many components can my PCB have? Each board can have no more than 200 components, and the total component quantity across the order cannot exceed 600. -Is there a limit on component types? Yes. The project can include no more than 100 different component types. -Are through-hole components allowed? Projects with through-hole components may qualify, provided that the total number of through-hole solder joints does not exceed 100 and all other requirements are met. -Can I apply the $29 price to multiple orders submitted at once? No. Only one eligible order can receive the promotional price when multiple orders are submitted together. -Can I use the offer again next month? The promotion may be available again according to the applicable monthly usage limit. Please check your eligibility before placing another order. -Does the $29 price cover my entire PCB project? The $29 offer is a special PCB assembly price, not necessarily the total cost of your project. PCB fabrication, components, shipping, and other applicable charges may be quoted separately. PCBWay's $29 PCB assembly offer is designed to make simple PCB prototypes more affordable. Check the eligibility requirements before ordering to ensure your project meets the technical limits and promotion rules. Ready to get started? Verify Now Blog > Analog vs Digital Circuits: Understanding Digital, Analog, and Mixed-Signal Chips Analog vs Digital Circuits: Understanding Digital, Analog, and Mixed-Signal Chips by: Mila Sep 30,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout analog vs digital circuits analog and digital circuits analog circuits digital circuits mixed signal PCB design We often say that the world of chips consists of only 0s and 1s. But more accurately, digital circuits use defined voltage ranges to represent discrete logic states, while the real world is clearly not like that. Human voices have different volumes, light has different levels of brightness, temperature changes continuously, and radio waves do not simply jump between 0 V and 1 V. So here is the question: If CPUs mainly process digital data, how can a smartphone hear sound, capture photos, connect to a cellular network, and charge its battery? The answer lies in three types of chips: digital chips, analog chips, and mixed-signal chips. Understanding the differences between them is also important for PCB layout , because digital, analog, and mixed-signal circuits have different requirements for signal integrity, grounding, power, and noise control. （class B analog audio amplifier） Analog vs Digital Circuits: What Is the Difference? The key difference between analog vs digital circuits is how they represent and process signals. Digital signals focus on discrete states. In a typical digital circuit, voltage is divided into high and low ranges, which are interpreted as 1 and 0. As long as the signal remains within the specified range, small amounts of noise usually do not change the logic result. Analog signals, on the other hand, preserve continuous changes. The small voltage generated by a microphone, the radio-frequency signal received by an antenna, changes in temperature detected by a sensor, and the voltage and current during battery charging and discharging can all vary continuously over time and amplitude. A simple way to understand analog and digital circuits is: A digital signal is like written text. It mainly cares about which character is being represented. An analog signal is like speech. It contains not only information, but also volume, tone, speed, and many subtle changes. In other words, digital circuits are good at processing discrete information, while analog circuits directly interact with continuously changing signals from the real world. （Analog vs Digital Signals） Digital Chips: Computing, Control, and Memory Digital chips are best suited to problems that can be clearly defined and represented as discrete data. Common digital chips include: CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs; MCUs and various controllers; DRAM, SRAM, and NAND Flash; FPGAs; Digital interface and network processing chips. Digital circuits are built from large numbers of logic gates, flip-flops, registers, and memory cells. Driven by a clock, data flows and is processed according to defined rules. Their biggest advantage is their high level of abstraction. Engineers can move from transistors to logic gates, then to adders, processors, instructions, and software. This allows complex systems to be designed, verified, and optimized at different levels of abstraction. Digital chips are particularly suitable for: Executing programs; Storing data; Implementing complex control functions; Performing large-scale logic and mathematical operations; Precisely coordinating different functions within a system. However, digital circuits themselves cannot directly process continuously changing analog signals. A CPU cannot simply take the tiny analog voltage generated by a microphone and process it as digital data. Nor can it directly turn a string of binary data into the continuous analog signal needed to drive a speaker. This is where analog circuits and mixed-signal circuits come in. Analog Chips: Connecting Electronics to the Real World Analog chips process continuously changing voltages and currents. They do not necessarily focus on extremely large amounts of digital logic, but they often determine whether a device can hear clearly, measure accurately, transmit effectively, and charge efficiently. Typical analog and analog-intensive chips include: Operational amplifiers and comparators; Voltage references and analog front ends; Power management chips such as LDOs and DC-DC converters; Audio amplifiers; Analog circuits used in RF front ends. The problems that analog circuits need to solve are very much connected to the real world: How do you amplify a weak signal? How do you filter out unwanted noise? How do you keep an output voltage stable? How do you maintain performance when temperature and supply voltage change? Analog design is challenging because many real-world details cannot simply be abstracted away. Transistor characteristics, temperature, noise, power-supply fluctuations, parasitic resistance, and parasitic capacitance can all affect the final result. Digital circuits mainly need to determine whether a signal should be recognized as 1 or 0, so many small variations can be tolerated. Analog circuits, however, often need to pay close attention to the actual signal amplitude, noise, distortion, and offset. For example, for an analog amplifier, whether the output is 0.999 V or 1.001 V may affect the final measurement or control result. Mixed-Signal Chips: Bridging the Analog and Digital Worlds Real-world electronic devices need both analog and digital processing. That is why mixed-signal chips exist. They integrate analog and digital circuits into the same chip or system so that the two types of circuits can work together. The most typical bridge is: ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter): Converts analog signals into digital data; DAC (Digital-to-Analog Converter): Converts digital data back into analog signals. The process can be simplified as: Real world → Analog signal → ADC → Digital data → Digital processing → DAC → Analog signal → Real world For example, during audio recording and playback, a microphone first converts sound into an analog electrical signal. The analog front end processes the signal, and an ADC converts it into digital data. After the digital processor stores and processes the data, a DAC converts it back into an analog signal, which is then amplified and reproduced by a speaker. A mixed-signal chip is not simply a combination of an ADC and a DAC. It may also contain: ADCs and DACs; PLLs and clock circuits; High-speed SerDes interfaces; Analog front ends; Digital calibration and control logic. These circuits need to work together within the same system, which is one reason mixed-signal design can be challenging. How Do Digital, Analog, and Mixed-Signal Chips Work Together in a Smartphone? A smartphone is a typical example of a system that combines all three types of chips. It needs to process digital data while constantly interacting with the analog signals of the real world. When You Take a Photo The image sensor converts light into electrical signals; The analog front end amplifies and processes the weak signals; The ADC converts the analog signals into digital data; The ISP performs noise reduction, white balance, and color processing; The CPU, GPU, NPU, and other digital processing units continue with computation, compression, display, and AI recognition. The overall process is essentially: Light → Analog electrical signal → Digital image data → Digital processing When You Connect to a Cellular Network The antenna receives radio-frequency signals; The RF front end amplifies, filters, and converts the signals; An ADC and related circuits convert the analog signal into digital samples; The baseband processor performs demodulation, error correction, and protocol processing. The signal path can be simplified as: Radio waves → Analog RF signal → Digital data → Baseband processing When You Charge Your Smartphone Power management and charging circuits convert and regulate the input voltage and current; The system monitors battery voltage, temperature, and charging status; Power devices handle the main energy conversion; Digital control logic adjusts the charging strategy according to system conditions. So, a smartphone is not purely a “digital device.” Digital, Analog, and Mixed-Signal Chips Compared These three types do not simply replace one another. In real electronic systems, they usually need to work together. Why Are Analog Chips Difficult to Replace? Many people see advanced digital chips with tens of billions of transistors and assume that analog chips must be relatively simple. In reality, the difficulty of analog design is not simply about transistor count. It lies in the trade-offs among device characteristics, process technology, noise, temperature, matching, and parasitic effects. Digital design can make extensive use of standard cells and automated tools. Analog circuits, however, often require repeated optimization based on process technology, device characteristics, and the application environment. The same circuit can behave differently when implemented on a different process. Even a seemingly insignificant trace in the layout can introduce additional parasitic effects, noise coupling, or matching problems. As a result, analog chip design often relies heavily on accumulated process and design experience, along with extensive verification and reliability testing. Why Do These Differences Matter in PCB Design? The differences between analog and digital circuits inside a chip also extend to PCB design. Digital circuits typically require careful consideration of signal integrity, crosstalk, clocks, and return paths, while analog circuits are more sensitive to noise, grounding, power stability, and sensitive signal integrity. For mixed signal PCB design, these issues often exist at the same time. For example, an ADC or DAC may connect to analog signals on one side and digital processing circuitry on the other. If the layout, power distribution, grounding, or return paths are not properly designed, noise generated by digital circuits can couple into sensitive analog signals. Therefore, mixed-signal PCB design often requires careful consideration of: Analog and digital circuit placement; Power and ground design; Return paths for high-speed digital signals; Noise control around ADCs and DACs; Decoupling capacitors and power integrity; Isolation between sensitive analog signals and high-speed digital signals. This is why understanding the differences between analog and digital circuits is important not only for chip designers, but also for PCB designers. Conclusion Digital chips have not replaced analog chips, and analog chips are not a “lower-end” version of digital chips. They serve different purposes: Digital chips handle computing, control, and memory. Analog chips handle sensing, amplification, and driving. Mixed-signal chips connect and translate between the two. Without digital chips, electronic devices would struggle to perform complex computations. Without analog chips, even the most powerful processor could not directly hear, see, sense, or interact with the real world. And in today's electronic devices, it is rarely one type of chip working alone. Instead, digital, analog, and mixed-signal circuits work together as one system. The smartphones, computers, vehicles, and smart devices we use every day are ultimately the result of these three worlds working together. Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Verify Now Blog > Analog vs Digital Circuits: Understanding Digital, Analog, and Mixed-Signal Chips Analog vs Digital Circuits: Understanding Digital, Analog, and Mixed-Signal Chips by: Mila Sep 30,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout analog vs digital circuits analog and digital circuits analog circuits digital circuits mixed signal PCB design We often say that the world of chips consists of only 0s and 1s. But more accurately, digital circuits use defined voltage ranges to represent discrete logic states, while the real world is clearly not like that. Human voices have different volumes, light has different levels of brightness, temperature changes continuously, and radio waves do not simply jump between 0 V and 1 V. So here is the question: If CPUs mainly process digital data, how can a smartphone hear sound, capture photos, connect to a cellular network, and charge its battery? The answer lies in three types of chips: digital chips, analog chips, and mixed-signal chips. Understanding the differences between them is also important for PCB layout , because digital, analog, and mixed-signal circuits have different requirements for signal integrity, grounding, power, and noise control. （class B analog audio amplifier） Analog vs Digital Circuits: What Is the Difference? The key difference between analog vs digital circuits is how they represent and process signals. Digital signals focus on discrete states. In a typical digital circuit, voltage is divided into high and low ranges, which are interpreted as 1 and 0. As long as the signal remains within the specified range, small amounts of noise usually do not change the logic result. Analog signals, on the other hand, preserve continuous changes. The small voltage generated by a microphone, the radio-frequency signal received by an antenna, changes in temperature detected by a sensor, and the voltage and current during battery charging and discharging can all vary continuously over time and amplitude. A simple way to understand analog and digital circuits is: A digital signal is like written text. It mainly cares about which character is being represented. An analog signal is like speech. It contains not only information, but also volume, tone, speed, and many subtle changes. In other words, digital circuits are good at processing discrete information, while analog circuits directly interact with continuously changing signals from the real world. （Analog vs Digital Signals） Digital Chips: Computing, Control, and Memory Digital chips are best suited to problems that can be clearly defined and represented as discrete data. Common digital chips include: CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs; MCUs and various controllers; DRAM, SRAM, and NAND Flash; FPGAs; Digital interface and network processing chips. Digital circuits are built from large numbers of logic gates, flip-flops, registers, and memory cells. Driven by a clock, data flows and is processed according to defined rules. Their biggest advantage is their high level of abstraction. Engineers can move from transistors to logic gates, then to adders, processors, instructions, and software. This allows complex systems to be designed, verified, and optimized at different levels of abstraction. Digital chips are particularly suitable for: Executing programs; Storing data; Implementing complex control functions; Performing large-scale logic and mathematical operations; Precisely coordinating different functions within a system. However, digital circuits themselves cannot directly process continuously changing analog signals. A CPU cannot simply take the tiny analog voltage generated by a microphone and process it as digital data. Nor can it directly turn a string of binary data into the continuous analog signal needed to drive a speaker. This is where analog circuits and mixed-signal circuits come in. Analog Chips: Connecting Electronics to the Real World Analog chips process continuously changing voltages and currents. They do not necessarily focus on extremely large amounts of digital logic, but they often determine whether a device can hear clearly, measure accurately, transmit effectively, and charge efficiently. Typical analog and analog-intensive chips include: Operational amplifiers and comparators; Voltage references and analog front ends; Power management chips such as LDOs and DC-DC converters; Audio amplifiers; Analog circuits used in RF front ends. The problems that analog circuits need to solve are very much connected to the real world: How do you amplify a weak signal? How do you filter out unwanted noise? How do you keep an output voltage stable? How do you maintain performance when temperature and supply voltage change? Analog design is challenging because many real-world details cannot simply be abstracted away. Transistor characteristics, temperature, noise, power-supply fluctuations, parasitic resistance, and parasitic capacitance can all affect the final result. Digital circuits mainly need to determine whether a signal should be recognized as 1 or 0, so many small variations can be tolerated. Analog circuits, however, often need to pay close attention to the actual signal amplitude, noise, distortion, and offset. For example, for an analog amplifier, whether the output is 0.999 V or 1.001 V may affect the final measurement or control result. Mixed-Signal Chips: Bridging the Analog and Digital Worlds Real-world electronic devices need both analog and digital processing. That is why mixed-signal chips exist. They integrate analog and digital circuits into the same chip or system so that the two types of circuits can work together. The most typical bridge is: ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter): Converts analog signals into digital data; DAC (Digital-to-Analog Converter): Converts digital data back into analog signals. The process can be simplified as: Real world → Analog signal → ADC → Digital data → Digital processing → DAC → Analog signal → Real world For example, during audio recording and playback, a microphone first converts sound into an analog electrical signal. The analog front end processes the signal, and an ADC converts it into digital data. After the digital processor stores and processes the data, a DAC converts it back into an analog signal, which is then amplified and reproduced by a speaker. A mixed-signal chip is not simply a combination of an ADC and a DAC. It may also contain: ADCs and DACs; PLLs and clock circuits; High-speed SerDes interfaces; Analog front ends; Digital calibration and control logic. These circuits need to work together within the same system, which is one reason mixed-signal design can be challenging. How Do Digital, Analog, and Mixed-Signal Chips Work Together in a Smartphone? A smartphone is a typical example of a system that combines all three types of chips. It needs to process digital data while constantly interacting with the analog signals of the real world. When You Take a Photo The image sensor converts light into electrical signals; The analog front end amplifies and processes the weak signals; The ADC converts the analog signals into digital data; The ISP performs noise reduction, white balance, and color processing; The CPU, GPU, NPU, and other digital processing units continue with computation, compression, display, and AI recognition. The overall process is essentially: Light → Analog electrical signal → Digital image data → Digital processing When You Connect to a Cellular Network The antenna receives radio-frequency signals; The RF front end amplifies, filters, and converts the signals; An ADC and related circuits convert the analog signal into digital samples; The baseband processor performs demodulation, error correction, and protocol processing. The signal path can be simplified as: Radio waves → Analog RF signal → Digital data → Baseband processing When You Charge Your Smartphone Power management and charging circuits convert and regulate the input voltage and current; The system monitors battery voltage, temperature, and charging status; Power devices handle the main energy conversion; Digital control logic adjusts the charging strategy according to system conditions. So, a smartphone is not purely a “digital device.” Digital, Analog, and Mixed-Signal Chips Compared These three types do not simply replace one another. In real electronic systems, they usually need to work together. Why Are Analog Chips Difficult to Replace? Many people see advanced digital chips with tens of billions of transistors and assume that analog chips must be relatively simple. In reality, the difficulty of analog design is not simply about transistor count. It lies in the trade-offs among device characteristics, process technology, noise, temperature, matching, and parasitic effects. Digital design can make extensive use of standard cells and automated tools. Analog circuits, however, often require repeated optimization based on process technology, device characteristics, and the application environment. The same circuit can behave differently when implemented on a different process. Even a seemingly insignificant trace in the layout can introduce additional parasitic effects, noise coupling, or matching problems. As a result, analog chip design often relies heavily on accumulated process and design experience, along with extensive verification and reliability testing. Why Do These Differences Matter in PCB Design? The differences between analog and digital circuits inside a chip also extend to PCB design. Digital circuits typically require careful consideration of signal integrity, crosstalk, clocks, and return paths, while analog circuits are more sensitive to noise, grounding, power stability, and sensitive signal integrity. For mixed signal PCB design, these issues often exist at the same time. For example, an ADC or DAC may connect to analog signals on one side and digital processing circuitry on the other. If the layout, power distribution, grounding, or return paths are not properly designed, noise generated by digital circuits can couple into sensitive analog signals. Therefore, mixed-signal PCB design often requires careful consideration of: Analog and digital circuit placement; Power and ground design; Return paths for high-speed digital signals; Noise control around ADCs and DACs; Decoupling capacitors and power integrity; Isolation between sensitive analog signals and high-speed digital signals. This is why understanding the differences between analog and digital circuits is important not only for chip designers, but also for PCB designers. Conclusion Digital chips have not replaced analog chips, and analog chips are not a “lower-end” version of digital chips. They serve different purposes: Digital chips handle computing, control, and memory. Analog chips handle sensing, amplification, and driving. Mixed-signal chips connect and translate between the two. Without digital chips, electronic devices would struggle to perform complex computations. Without analog chips, even the most powerful processor could not directly hear, see, sense, or interact with the real world. And in today's electronic devices, it is rarely one type of chip working alone. Instead, digital, analog, and mixed-signal circuits work together as one system. The smartphones, computers, vehicles, and smart devices we use every day are ultimately the result of these three worlds working together. Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Typical analog and analog-intensive chips include: Operational amplifiers and comparators; Voltage references and analog front ends; Power management chips such as LDOs and DC-DC converters; Audio amplifiers; Analog circuits used in RF front ends. The problems that analog circuits need to solve are very much connected to the real world: How do you amplify a weak signal? How do you filter out unwanted noise? How do you keep an output voltage stable? How do you maintain performance when temperature and supply voltage change? Analog design is challenging because many real-world details cannot simply be abstracted away. Transistor characteristics, temperature, noise, power-supply fluctuations, parasitic resistance, and parasitic capacitance can all affect the final result. Digital circuits mainly need to determine whether a signal should be recognized as 1 or 0, so many small variations can be tolerated. Analog circuits, however, often need to pay close attention to the actual signal amplitude, noise, distortion, and offset. For example, for an analog amplifier, whether the output is 0.999 V or 1.001 V may affect the final measurement or control result. Mixed-Signal Chips: Bridging the Analog and Digital Worlds Real-world electronic devices need both analog and digital processing. That is why mixed-signal chips exist. They integrate analog and digital circuits into the same chip or system so that the two types of circuits can work together. The most typical bridge is: ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter): Converts analog signals into digital data; DAC (Digital-to-Analog Converter): Converts digital data back into analog signals. The process can be simplified as: Real world → Analog signal → ADC → Digital data → Digital processing → DAC → Analog signal → Real world For example, during audio recording and playback, a microphone first converts sound into an analog electrical signal. The analog front end processes the signal, and an ADC converts it into digital data. After the digital processor stores and processes the data, a DAC converts it back into an analog signal, which is then amplified and reproduced by a speaker. A mixed-signal chip is not simply a combination of an ADC and a DAC. It may also contain: ADCs and DACs; PLLs and clock circuits; High-speed SerDes interfaces; Analog front ends; Digital calibration and control logic. These circuits need to work together within the same system, which is one reason mixed-signal design can be challenging. How Do Digital, Analog, and Mixed-Signal Chips Work Together in a Smartphone? A smartphone is a typical example of a system that combines all three types of chips. It needs to process digital data while constantly interacting with the analog signals of the real world. When You Take a Photo The image sensor converts light into electrical signals; The analog front end amplifies and processes the weak signals; The ADC converts the analog signals into digital data; The ISP performs noise reduction, white balance, and color processing; The CPU, GPU, NPU, and other digital processing units continue with computation, compression, display, and AI recognition. The overall process is essentially: Light → Analog electrical signal → Digital image data → Digital processing When You Connect to a Cellular Network The antenna receives radio-frequency signals; The RF front end amplifies, filters, and converts the signals; An ADC and related circuits convert the analog signal into digital samples; The baseband processor performs demodulation, error correction, and protocol processing. So, a smartphone is not purely a “digital device.” Digital, Analog, and Mixed-Signal Chips Compared These three types do not simply replace one another. Many people see advanced digital chips with tens of billions of transistors and assume that analog chips must be relatively simple. In reality, the difficulty of analog design is not simply about transistor count. It lies in the trade-offs among device characteristics, process technology, noise, temperature, matching, and parasitic effects. Digital design can make extensive use of standard cells and automated tools. Analog circuits, however, often require repeated optimization based on process technology, device characteristics, and the application environment. The same circuit can behave differently when implemented on a different process. Even a seemingly insignificant trace in the layout can introduce additional parasitic effects, noise coupling, or matching problems. As a result, analog chip design often relies heavily on accumulated process and design experience, along with extensive verification and reliability testing. Digital circuits typically require careful consideration of signal integrity, crosstalk, clocks, and return paths, while analog circuits are more sensitive to noise, grounding, power stability, and sensitive signal integrity. Without digital chips, electronic devices would struggle to perform complex computations. Without analog chips, even the most powerful processor could not directly hear, see, sense, or interact with the real world. And in today's electronic devices, it is rarely one type of chip working alone. Instead, digital, analog, and mixed-signal circuits work together as one system. Verify Now Blog > Analog vs Digital Circuits: Understanding Digital, Analog, and Mixed-Signal Chips Analog vs Digital Circuits: Understanding Digital, Analog, and Mixed-Signal Chips by: Mila Sep 30,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout analog vs digital circuits analog and digital circuits analog circuits digital circuits mixed signal PCB design We often say that the world of chips consists of only 0s and 1s. But more accurately, digital circuits use defined voltage ranges to represent discrete logic states, while the real world is clearly not like that. Human voices have different volumes, light has different levels of brightness, temperature changes continuously, and radio waves do not simply jump between 0 V and 1 V. So here is the question: If CPUs mainly process digital data, how can a smartphone hear sound, capture photos, connect to a cellular network, and charge its battery? The answer lies in three types of chips: digital chips, analog chips, and mixed-signal chips. Understanding the differences between them is also important for PCB layout , because digital, analog, and mixed-signal circuits have different requirements for signal integrity, grounding, power, and noise control. （class B analog audio amplifier） Analog vs Digital Circuits: What Is the Difference? The key difference between analog vs digital circuits is how they represent and process signals. Digital signals focus on discrete states. In a typical digital circuit, voltage is divided into high and low ranges, which are interpreted as 1 and 0. As long as the signal remains within the specified range, small amounts of noise usually do not change the logic result. Analog signals, on the other hand, preserve continuous changes. The small voltage generated by a microphone, the radio-frequency signal received by an antenna, changes in temperature detected by a sensor, and the voltage and current during battery charging and discharging can all vary continuously over time and amplitude. A simple way to understand analog and digital circuits is: A digital signal is like written text. It mainly cares about which character is being represented. An analog signal is like speech. It contains not only information, but also volume, tone, speed, and many subtle changes. In other words, digital circuits are good at processing discrete information, while analog circuits directly interact with continuously changing signals from the real world. （Analog vs Digital Signals） Digital Chips: Computing, Control, and Memory Digital chips are best suited to problems that can be clearly defined and represented as discrete data. Common digital chips include: CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs; MCUs and various controllers; DRAM, SRAM, and NAND Flash; FPGAs; Digital interface and network processing chips. Digital circuits are built from large numbers of logic gates, flip-flops, registers, and memory cells. Driven by a clock, data flows and is processed according to defined rules. Their biggest advantage is their high level of abstraction. Engineers can move from transistors to logic gates, then to adders, processors, instructions, and software. This allows complex systems to be designed, verified, and optimized at different levels of abstraction. Digital chips are particularly suitable for: Executing programs; Storing data; Implementing complex control functions; Performing large-scale logic and mathematical operations; Precisely coordinating different functions within a system. However, digital circuits themselves cannot directly process continuously changing analog signals. A CPU cannot simply take the tiny analog voltage generated by a microphone and process it as digital data. Nor can it directly turn a string of binary data into the continuous analog signal needed to drive a speaker. This is where analog circuits and mixed-signal circuits come in. Analog Chips: Connecting Electronics to the Real World Analog chips process continuously changing voltages and currents. They do not necessarily focus on extremely large amounts of digital logic, but they often determine whether a device can hear clearly, measure accurately, transmit effectively, and charge efficiently. Typical analog and analog-intensive chips include: Operational amplifiers and comparators; Voltage references and analog front ends; Power management chips such as LDOs and DC-DC converters; Audio amplifiers; Analog circuits used in RF front ends. The problems that analog circuits need to solve are very much connected to the real world: How do you amplify a weak signal? How do you filter out unwanted noise? How do you keep an output voltage stable? How do you maintain performance when temperature and supply voltage change? Analog design is challenging because many real-world details cannot simply be abstracted away. Transistor characteristics, temperature, noise, power-supply fluctuations, parasitic resistance, and parasitic capacitance can all affect the final result. Digital circuits mainly need to determine whether a signal should be recognized as 1 or 0, so many small variations can be tolerated. Analog circuits, however, often need to pay close attention to the actual signal amplitude, noise, distortion, and offset. For example, for an analog amplifier, whether the output is 0.999 V or 1.001 V may affect the final measurement or control result. Mixed-Signal Chips: Bridging the Analog and Digital Worlds Real-world electronic devices need both analog and digital processing. That is why mixed-signal chips exist. They integrate analog and digital circuits into the same chip or system so that the two types of circuits can work together. The most typical bridge is: ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter): Converts analog signals into digital data; DAC (Digital-to-Analog Converter): Converts digital data back into analog signals. The process can be simplified as: Real world → Analog signal → ADC → Digital data → Digital processing → DAC → Analog signal → Real world For example, during audio recording and playback, a microphone first converts sound into an analog electrical signal. The analog front end processes the signal, and an ADC converts it into digital data. After the digital processor stores and processes the data, a DAC converts it back into an analog signal, which is then amplified and reproduced by a speaker. A mixed-signal chip is not simply a combination of an ADC and a DAC. It may also contain: ADCs and DACs; PLLs and clock circuits; High-speed SerDes interfaces; Analog front ends; Digital calibration and control logic. These circuits need to work together within the same system, which is one reason mixed-signal design can be challenging. How Do Digital, Analog, and Mixed-Signal Chips Work Together in a Smartphone? A smartphone is a typical example of a system that combines all three types of chips. It needs to process digital data while constantly interacting with the analog signals of the real world. When You Take a Photo The image sensor converts light into electrical signals; The analog front end amplifies and processes the weak signals; The ADC converts the analog signals into digital data; The ISP performs noise reduction, white balance, and color processing; The CPU, GPU, NPU, and other digital processing units continue with computation, compression, display, and AI recognition. The overall process is essentially: Light → Analog electrical signal → Digital image data → Digital processing When You Connect to a Cellular Network The antenna receives radio-frequency signals; The RF front end amplifies, filters, and converts the signals; An ADC and related circuits convert the analog signal into digital samples; The baseband processor performs demodulation, error correction, and protocol processing. The signal path can be simplified as: Radio waves → Analog RF signal → Digital data → Baseband processing When You Charge Your Smartphone Power management and charging circuits convert and regulate the input voltage and current; The system monitors battery voltage, temperature, and charging status; Power devices handle the main energy conversion; Digital control logic adjusts the charging strategy according to system conditions. So, a smartphone is not purely a “digital device.” Digital, Analog, and Mixed-Signal Chips Compared These three types do not simply replace one another. In real electronic systems, they usually need to work together. Why Are Analog Chips Difficult to Replace? Many people see advanced digital chips with tens of billions of transistors and assume that analog chips must be relatively simple. In reality, the difficulty of analog design is not simply about transistor count. It lies in the trade-offs among device characteristics, process technology, noise, temperature, matching, and parasitic effects. Digital design can make extensive use of standard cells and automated tools. Analog circuits, however, often require repeated optimization based on process technology, device characteristics, and the application environment. The same circuit can behave differently when implemented on a different process. Even a seemingly insignificant trace in the layout can introduce additional parasitic effects, noise coupling, or matching problems. As a result, analog chip design often relies heavily on accumulated process and design experience, along with extensive verification and reliability testing. Why Do These Differences Matter in PCB Design? The differences between analog and digital circuits inside a chip also extend to PCB design. Digital circuits typically require careful consideration of signal integrity, crosstalk, clocks, and return paths, while analog circuits are more sensitive to noise, grounding, power stability, and sensitive signal integrity. For mixed signal PCB design, these issues often exist at the same time. For example, an ADC or DAC may connect to analog signals on one side and digital processing circuitry on the other. If the layout, power distribution, grounding, or return paths are not properly designed, noise generated by digital circuits can couple into sensitive analog signals. Therefore, mixed-signal PCB design often requires careful consideration of: Analog and digital circuit placement; Power and ground design; Return paths for high-speed digital signals; Noise control around ADCs and DACs; Decoupling capacitors and power integrity; Isolation between sensitive analog signals and high-speed digital signals. This is why understanding the differences between analog and digital circuits is important not only for chip designers, but also for PCB designers. Conclusion Digital chips have not replaced analog chips, and analog chips are not a “lower-end” version of digital chips. They serve different purposes: Digital chips handle computing, control, and memory. Analog chips handle sensing, amplification, and driving. Mixed-signal chips connect and translate between the two. Without digital chips, electronic devices would struggle to perform complex computations. Without analog chips, even the most powerful processor could not directly hear, see, sense, or interact with the real world. And in today's electronic devices, it is rarely one type of chip working alone. Instead, digital, analog, and mixed-signal circuits work together as one system. The smartphones, computers, vehicles, and smart devices we use every day are ultimately the result of these three worlds working together. Enter the year of your birth and check your Chinese Zodiac. Are More PCB Decoupling Capacitors Always Better? by: Mila Oct 12,2026 <dynamic-value> <dynamic-value> Posted in PCB Design & Layout decoupling capacitor PCB decoupling capacitor decoupling capacitor placement PCB power integrity If you have ever designed a PCB schematic , you have probably placed a familiar trio of capacitors near a chip’s power pins: 0.1 µF, 1 µF, and 10 µF.It seems like a safe bet. Different capacitance values, neatly arranged, ready to keep the power supply stable and suppress noise. But is this tried-and-tested combination always the best choice? When it comes to decoupling capacitors, does adding more always mean better performance? Not necessarily. Effective decoupling depends on more than capacitance alone. Component characteristics, parasitic effects, and PCB layout all play a role. Understanding ESR, ESL, and Self-Resonant Frequenc Circuit theory tells us that the impedance of an ideal capacitor decreases as frequency increases. Real capacitors, however, are not quite so simple. They have two important parasitic parameters: equivalent series resistance (ESR) and equivalent series inductance (ESL). ESL deserves particular attention. As frequency increases, the capacitive impedance decreases until the capacitor reaches its self-resonant frequency (SRF). Around this frequency, the capacitor typically exhibits its minimum impedance. Beyond SRF, parasitic inductance begins to dominate, and impedance increases with frequency. In other words, a capacitor does not become more effective at filtering noise simply because the frequency keeps rising. Above its SRF, its ability to suppress higher-frequency noise may be limited. That is why selecting a PCB decoupling capacitor requires more than checking its nominal capacitance. You also need to understand how its impedance changes with frequency. How Different Capacitance Values Work Together Capacitors with different capacitance values have different impedance characteristics. When selected appropriately, they can help maintain low impedance across a wider frequency range in the power distribution network (PDN). 10 µF capacitors are commonly used to provide local charge storage and help reduce impedance over certain low- to mid-frequency ranges. Their actual performance depends on the capacitor type, package, ESR, ESL, and operating voltage. For lower-frequency ripple, the voltage regulator, bulk capacitors, and the overall power network must also be considered. 1 µF capacitors can complement larger and smaller capacitors by helping shape the impedance response over particular frequency ranges. However, whether they effectively fill the gap between other capacitance values depends on the actual impedance curves, not just the nominal capacitance. 0.1 µF capacitors are commonly used for high-frequency decoupling near chip power pins. Component characteristics, parasitic effects, and PCB layout all play a role. Understanding ESR, ESL, and Self-Resonant Frequenc Circuit theory tells us that the impedance of an ideal capacitor decreases as frequency increases. Real capacitors, however, are not quite so simple. They have two important parasitic parameters: equivalent series resistance (ESR) and equivalent series inductance (ESL). ESL deserves particular attention. As frequency increases, the capacitive impedance decreases until the capacitor reaches its self-resonant frequency (SRF). Around this frequency, the capacitor typically exhibits its minimum impedance. Beyond SRF, parasitic inductance begins to dominate, and impedance increases with frequency. In other words, a capacitor does not become more effective at filtering noise simply because the frequency keeps rising. Above its SRF, its ability to suppress higher-frequency noise may be limited. That is why selecting a PCB decoupling capacitor requires more than checking its nominal capacitance. You also need to understand how its impedance changes with frequency. How Different Capacitance Values Work Together Capacitors with different capacitance values have different impedance characteristics. When selected appropriately, they can help maintain low impedance across a wider frequency range in the power distribution network (PDN). 10 µF capacitors are commonly used to provide local charge storage and help reduce impedance over certain low- to mid-frequency ranges. Their actual performance depends on the capacitor type, package, ESR, ESL, and operating voltage. For lower-frequency ripple, the voltage regulator, bulk capacitors, and the overall power network must also be considered. 1 µF capacitors can complement larger and smaller capacitors by helping shape the impedance response over particular frequency ranges. However, whether they effectively fill the gap between other capacitance values depends on the actual impedance curves, not just the nominal capacitance. 0.1 µF capacitors are commonly used for high-frequency decoupling near chip power pins. Although their capacitance is smaller, they can often be placed in compact packages with short connection paths, helping reduce parasitic inductance and improve high-frequency decoupling performance. Each has its strengths, and combining them can make sense. However, 10 µF, 1 µF, and 0.1 µF are not a universal combination with three fixed frequency ranges. Once operating conditions come into play, its capacitance may change significantly with temperature and DC bias voltage. That does not mean these dielectric types are unsuitable for every application. However, their characteristics may make them less suitable for decoupling applications that require stable capacitance. For common power supply decoupling applications, X7R and X5R are often preferred dielectric types. But choosing either one does not guarantee that the nominal capacitance will be available under operating conditions. Multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs), especially those with high capacitance in small packages, can experience significant capacitance loss under DC bias.
